title: The Young Ascetic Had No Name
source: Valmiki Ramayana, Ayodhya Kanda 2.57-58 (Critical Edition; vulgate 2.63-64)

captions.instagram:
We all know the story of Shravan Kumar, the son who carried his blind parents on a pilgrimage. In Valmiki's Ramayana (Critical Edition, Ayodhya 2.57-58), King Dasharatha tells the story himself to Kausalya, at midnight, on the night he dies. The young man is never named: Valmiki calls him only "the ascetic" and "the sage's son". There is no pilgrimage and no kavad: he came alone to the Sarayu at night to fetch water for his blind parents. He asked Dasharatha to pull out the arrow and tell his father, and after death he rose to heaven in divine form. Tulsidas too writes only "तापस अंध साप सुधि आई". Both tellings are told with devotion.

Did you know the boy is never named in Valmiki? Where did you first hear 'Shravan Kumar'? 👇 Jai Shri Ram!

📜 Source: Valmiki Ramayana, Ayodhya Kanda 2.57-58 (Critical Edition; vulgate 2.63-64)

We all know the story of Shravan Kumar, the son who carried his blind parents on a pilgrimage. Did you know the boy is never named in Valmiki? Where did you first hear 'Shravan Kumar'? 👇 Jai Shri Ram!

Source: Valmiki Ramayana, Ayodhya Kanda 2.57-58 (Critical Edition; vulgate 2.63-64)
Verses:
• Dasharatha tells the story himself, to Kausalya, at midnight, remembering his old misdeed — 2.57.3
• Then Kausalya was not yet married and he was the crown prince; it was the rainy season — 2.57.10
• Hunting at night on the Sarayu he heard a sound like a pot filling, took it for an elephant and shot at the sound — 2.57.14-17; 2.58.13
• The young man came alone to the river at night for water; his parents were in their ashram (no pilgrimage, no kavad) — 2.57.19; 2.57.29; 2.57.35; 2.58.2-4
• He grieves not for himself but for his blind parents, who wait thirsty; one arrow kills all three — 2.57.23; 2.57.30-31
• He asks Dasharatha to tell his father and to pull out the arrow; Dasharatha does, and he dies — 2.57.34-39
• The young man is never named in Valmiki: only तापस / तपस्विन् / मुनिपुत्र / 'your son' (whole of CE 2.57-58 read; parents unnamed too) — 2.57-58 (whole episode)
• Ramcharitmanas: 'तापस अंध साप सुधि आई। कौसल्यहि सब कथा सुनाई।।' (no name given) — Ramcharitmanas, Ayodhya Kand, chaupai before doha 155
